samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments`'s `dropArchives` option is never exercised against the real implementation, so the archive-purge on lost workspace access is uncovered
samples.evidence: `api/workspaces.ts:136,167` call `purgeOfflineDocuments(doomed, { dropArchives: true })` — the mechanism that removes archived full-document snapshots when a workspace is deleted or the signed-in member is removed. `workspaces.test.ts:15-16` mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale, so its five `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith([...], { dropArchives: true })` assertions only prove the argument is forwarded to a stub. `offline-erase.test.ts`'s "a document that was deleted" block (lines 667-703) is the only place the real `purgeOfflineDocuments` runs, and every call there omits the option (`purgeOfflineDocuments(["abc"])`, `(["keep"])`, `(["anon"])`); one of them asserts the *opposite* ("keeps the archives", line 680). Grep for `dropArchives` across `packages/frontend/src` returns only the two call sites, the mocked assertions, and the two lines of the implementation. If the `options.dropArchives ? "drop" : "keep"` mapping at offline-erase.ts:405 were wrong, archives of a workspace the user was removed from would stay on disk and `recoverOfflineCopy` would re-materialize that content as a document the user owns — the exact privacy rule the feature states — with every suite green.

samples.summary: No test renders the real lapse publishers, so which `DurabilityLapse` each one emits — and which scope wins when both are mounted — is uncovered
samples.evidence: `useDurabilityLapse` has exactly two producers: `collab-document-provider.tsx:350` (`unsupported`/`not-permitted`/`not-enabled`/`another-tab`) and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238` (`dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed`/`unreportable`). Grepping `DurabilityLapseScope|useDurabilityLapse` across packages/frontend shows the only test usage is `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632,865-869`, which hand-mounts the scopes with literal lapse values. So every "tooltip names which case applies" assertion (lines 783-841) and the `strandedUnderScopes` block (845-880) passes regardless of what the production components compute. Concretely uncovered: (a) the nesting order at collab-document-provider.tsx:350 — the comment there records that this scope was once mounted *inside* `inner`, which silently swallowed every durable-client reason; re-inverting it today fails no test, because the chip test supplies its own correctly-ordered scopes; (b) `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:164-169`, the `QuotaExceededError → setOutOfSpace(true)` branch, whose only observable effect is the `out-of-space` lapse — `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` fires `onWriteFailure(new Error('refused'))` and asserts only `useDocumentDurability()`, never the lapse; (c) that the share-link route actually publishes `not-permitted`, which is what the chip's offer-suppression (`sync-status-chip.tsx:99`) keys on.

samples.summary: The `saved-locally` tooltip sentence — the copy for this feature's headline new state — is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: `tooltipFor`'s `saved-locally` arm (sync-status-tooltip.ts:59-75) is new in this diff. Grepping `tooltipFor|saved-locally` in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` shows only `tooltipFor('not-saved', …)` (line 784) and `tooltipFor('saved', …)` (line 836). The `SyncStatusChip on a durable document` block (line 672 onward) never opens the tooltip — its "says where the work went" case asserts the *toast* description via `info.mock.calls`. Two further branches of the same function are also unasserted: the `connected: true` wording of `not-saved` ("were rejected by the server") — the `stranded()` helper hardcodes `connected: false` — and the `offerOffline` sentence at line 103, which the DOM tests cannot reach because `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` defaults to the pinned `0.7.22` there, making `supportsClientKey()` false.
searchedFor: grep tooltipFor|saved-locally|rejected by the server in tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx

samples.summary: The `saved-locally` toast's `warned.current` latch and its retraction/confirmation on recovery are untested
samples.evidence: sync-status-chip.tsx:190 sets `warned.current = true` inside the new `savedLocally` arm, with a comment claiming "the recovery arm below retracts this one too and confirms once the work actually reaches the server". The `SyncStatusChip on a durable document` describe (tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:672-…) only asserts the toast is raised; no case transitions a durable document back to `saved` and asserts `toast.dismiss(TOAST_ID)` plus the `Saved` success toast. Removing that one line would leave a stale "Saved to this device" toast on screen after the work reaches the server, with every test green.

samples.summary: `dropAllForUser`'s `keepArchives` option and `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` parameter have no caller and no test
samples.evidence: Grepping `keepArchives|onlyUser` across `packages/frontend/src` finds `keepArchives` only in its two declarations (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1123, offline-erase.ts:30) and the one `if (!options.keepArchives)` branch at 1161 — no call site ever passes it, and no test in `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` or `offline-erase.test.ts` sets it. The lengthy comment at 1154-1160 justifies it for "a session the server expired", but this diff's 401 arm (`api/auth.ts`, `eraseLocalData: "none"`) erases nothing at all, so the branch is unreachable. Likewise `dropArchivesWhere`'s third parameter `onlyUser` (line 1351) is never supplied by either call site (1162, 1232), so its documented per-account narrowing is never executed.

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser`'s skip of another account's orphaned snapshot is never exercised
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys` (line 1295) filters with `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)`, whose regex matches the `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` shape. The only orphan test — `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts`, "an entry that predates the header rule / is collected rather than living forever out of reach" — seeds the key `"doc-a"`, which matches no `wb:` prefix and therefore always takes the *not*-another-user path. I found no test that seeds an orphan under `pk/wb:{secret}:{otherUser}:{docKey}` and asserts it survives the sweep, so the guard could be inverted or always-false without any failure.

samples.summary: The claim that local cleanup can never fail an accepted deletion is untested — the test mocks the cleanup and never makes it reject
samples.evidence: `deleteDocument` (documents.ts:167) and `deleteDocuments` (215) both `await purgeOfflineDocuments(...)` after the server has accepted, with the comment "never able to turn an accepted deletion into a reported failure". `documents.test.ts:5` mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` with a bare `vi.fn()` that always resolves, so no case makes it reject and observes that `deleteDocument` still resolves. The real `purgeOfflineDocuments` does swallow internally (offline-erase.ts try/catch), but nothing pins that either: `offline-erase.test.ts`'s purge block has no case where the store throws. The equivalent property *is* tested for `deleteWorkspace` ("still deletes when the listing fails"), so the asymmetry looks like an oversight.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts 'a document that was deleted' block

samples.summary: "subscribes from inside the DocumentProvider, not above it" asserts synchronously after waiting only on the mount, which its sibling test documents as flaky
samples.evidence: The sibling case "latches on the SDK's dropped-changes event" waits on `subscribers.length === 1` and explains why: "`mounted` is pushed to during render, and the watch subscribes from an effect one level below — so waiting on the mount alone fires the event into an empty handler list often enough to fail roughly one run in five." This case does exactly that — `await waitFor(() => expect(mounted.length).toBe(1))` followed by a synchronous `expect(subscribers.length).toBe(1)` — so by the file's own reasoning it can intermittently fail (or, under a future change, pass for the wrong reason). Wrapping the subscriber count in the `waitFor` would make it deterministic.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx 'telling the store which removals are losses' block

finding.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments`'s `dropArchives` option is never exercised against the real implementation, so the archive-purge on lost workspace access is uncovered
finding.evidence: `api/workspaces.ts:136,167` call `purgeOfflineDocuments(doomed, { dropArchives: true })` — the mechanism that removes archived full-document snapshots when a workspace is deleted or the signed-in member is removed. `workspaces.test.ts:15-16` mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale, so its five `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith([...], { dropArchives: true })` assertions only prove the argument is forwarded to a stub. `offline-erase.test.ts`'s "a document that was deleted" block (lines 667-703) is the only place the real `purgeOfflineDocuments` runs, and every call there omits the option (`purgeOfflineDocuments(["abc"])`, `(["keep"])`, `(["anon"])`); one of them asserts the *opposite* ("keeps the archives", line 680). Grep for `dropArchives` across `packages/frontend/src` returns only the two call sites, the mocked assertions, and the two lines of the implementation. If the `options.dropArchives ? "drop" : "keep"` mapping at offline-erase.ts:405 were wrong, archives of a workspace the user was removed from would stay on disk and `recoverOfflineCopy` would re-materialize that content as a document the user owns — the exact privacy rule the feature states — with every suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `deleteWorkspace` (workspaces.ts:136) and `removeMember` (workspaces.ts:167) pass `{ dropArchives: true }`, and the option is consumed by the single mapping at offline-erase.ts:404-406. No test anywhere exercises that mapping against the real implementation: workspaces.test.ts:14-16 mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale so its five `toHaveBeenCalledWith(..., { dropArchives: true })` assertions only verify forwarding to a stub; the only real-implementation calls (offline-erase.test.ts:675, 690, 700) all omit the option, and 680-693 asserts the opposite branch (archives kept). I searched wider than the reviewer: repo-wide greps including packages/frontend/tests (only tests/api/auth.test.ts:87, another mock); api/url.test.ts:100-101 does invoke the real deleteWorkspace/removeMember unmocked, but with no remembered offline user and an empty id list it exits at the guard (offline-erase.ts:397-400) and asserts only URL segmentation (url.test.ts:162-174); workspace-settings.test.tsx:28-36 mocks @/api/workspaces. The store-level `{ archives: "drop" }` tests (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:718,744,959,971) cover the callee, not the option mapping. `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` archive-drop coverage (offline-erase.test.ts:520-537,551-566) is a different function and only narrows the exposure window. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a major gap: if the mapping regressed, archives of a workspace the user lost access to would persist and `recoverOfflineCopy` could re-materialize them as a document the user owns, with every suite green.

finding.evidence: `useDurabilityLapse` has exactly two producers: `collab-document-provider.tsx:350` (`unsupported`/`not-permitted`/`not-enabled`/`another-tab`) and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238` (`dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed`/`unreportable`). So every "tooltip names which case applies" assertion (lines 783-841) and the `strandedUnderScopes` block (845-880) passes regardless of what the production components compute. verdict.reason: No test observes a lapse produced by either real publisher. `useDurabilityLapse` has exactly one consumer (`sync-status-chip.tsx:79`), so the only way to observe a published lapse is to render `SyncStatusChip` under real providers. The only file mounting `DurabilityLapseScope` in tests is `sync-status-chip.test.tsx`, which supplies literal values (:632, :865-869); the tooltip cases at :783-840 call `tooltipFor` directly. The two other chip-bearing test files mock the chip out entirely (shared-header-status.test.tsx:11, site-header-sync-status.test.tsx:19). Tests that DO render the real publishers assert other properties: collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx checks clientKey/store/election only; durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx probes only useDocumentDurability() and fires a plain Error at :183/:237, never a QuotaExceededError DOMException, so the `out-of-space` branch at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:164-169 is never entered or observed; shared-document-durability.test.tsx mocks CollabDocumentProvider (:24-31) and stops at useDurabilityPermitted(), never at the `not-permitted` lapse the chip's offer-suppression keys on. Repo-wide grep for the distinguishing tooltip sentences finds them only in the source, the one chip test, and docs; there is no e2e/hunt oracle covering them. One caveat: since DurabilityLapseScope inherits (durable-document-context.ts:147-152), the nesting-order sub-claim (a) is weaker than stated, but sub-claims (b) and (c) are real, user-visible, and untested.
